Task: update the documentation for the Crustdata reply and the final claims check. Touch ONLY README.md. Never read .env or print environment variables or keys. Rules: every statement must come from a file you read or from the facts below; list anything you cannot back under CLAIMS I COULD NOT VERIFY; no marketing language; no secrets or codes.
Facts (from the builder): on 12 October 2026 we asked the Crustdata team whether our use is permitted: an invite-only demo app that runs company search and enrichment through their API with our own key and shows results to a handful of invited testers (hackathon judges and people we choose), results shown in the invited user's browser for the session only, only run counts and costs kept, and we asked whether attribution or field restrictions apply. The Crustdata team replied the same day that this is fine and that the only thing they prohibit is downloading their data as-is and bulk-selling it as a dataset. The reply is an informal message, not a signed agreement. Our question did not mention that company facts are sent to a third-party model provider inside the assessment prompts, nor a public demo video; a follow-up message about both was sent.
Edits: (1) Replace every statement that third-party display of Crustdata records waits for Crustdata's written confirmation with the facts above, including that the reply is informal and that the follow-up is pending. (2) In the Status paragraph: live codes may be issued by the builders to invited testers, including judges, on request; the public demo code is synthetic; live mode stays off by default and no live code is enabled at the time of writing. (3) Replace the wording 'no company data stored' (wherever it appears) with exactly: The application database stores no company records, only counts and costs. During a live run, the search criteria and company identifiers are sent to Crustdata, and company facts from the results are sent to the model provider in the assessment prompts. Results are returned only to the requesting browser, and our code does not log them. (4) In the Tested subsection and wherever the current test count is stated as 741, use the current numbers: 808 passed and 6 skipped (the 6 skipped are the Postgres integration tests that need TEST_DATABASE_URL). Do not change the historical build-log entry in hackathon.md. (5) In the limitations list add: our first question to Crustdata did not mention the model provider or a public demo video; a follow-up was sent and its reply is pending. (6) Add one sentence to the Live beta section: the application has no export or download feature, shows at most 10 companies per run, and each live code is capped at a few runs. Keep every other statement. Run no commands except git status. End with a plain-text SHORT REVIEW REPORT (under 20 lines, no code fences, no secrets): what changed with line numbers, CLAIMS I COULD NOT VERIFY, and anything you were unsure about.
</pasted_content id="5d25">

1	# SignalScout
2	
3	SignalScout is a prospecting agent that checks its data and its own claims before it spends money or writes outreach.
4	
5	## What it does
6	
7	Given an ideal customer profile (ICP), the agent runs these steps:
8	
9	1. **ICP.** The ICP (industry, employee-count ranges, locations, keywords, excluded domains) becomes search filters and assessment criteria.
10	2. **Search.** It searches a company provider (synthetic fixtures, or Crustdata) up to a result cap.
11	3. **Validate and deduplicate.** Code rules check every record. Rejected records and later duplicates are dropped before any paid enrichment (improved pipeline).
12	4. **Enrich the best candidates within caps.** Valid records are enriched first, up to the enrichment cap.
13	5. **Build facts.** Each field becomes a fact with a status and a provider.
14	6. **Assess from facts only.** The model scores the company against the criteria using the facts it is given.
15	7. **Check claims.** Code checks the assessment and any outreach draft against the facts. Outreach that fails is suppressed.
16	
17	Two pipelines exist: `baseline` (no pre-enrichment filtering, no guards) and `improved` (validation first, fact-based prompt, guards).
18	
19	## Results
20	
21	### Fixture runs
22	
23	Source: `evidence/summary.json`. Scenario: Synthetic fixtures with known defects, claude-haiku at temperature 0, 10 searched and 5 enriched in both runs. Run labels: `baseline-final`, `improved-final`. Provider cost basis: simulated at measured Crustdata prices.

102	Notes:
103	
104	- One run per pipeline on 10 live records, so this is a small sample, not a benchmark.
105	- The same three companies were flagged in both runs by a zero-tolerance size rule whose magnitude was not analysed (see the caveat in the live-data section).
106	- Cited but not citeable means the model cited a fact id that is not one of our fact ids for that company; it can mean an invented field or a different field name.
107	- Per assessment the improved prompt costs more; the total is lower because only enriched companies are assessed.
108	
109	## How the guards work
110	
111	### Validation rules (`src/core/data/validation.ts`)
112	
113	Deterministic and pure. Each record gets a status of `valid`, `flagged` or `rejected`, with issues by code:
114	
115	| Issue code | Meaning |
116	|---|---|
117	| `missing_name` | No company name. |
118	| `missing_domain` | No primary domain. |
119	| `junk_website` | Website is a messaging, link-shortener or social host (for example `wa.me`, `bit.ly`, `linktr.ee`). |
120	| `missing_linkedin` | No LinkedIn page. |
121	| `duplicate_domain` | Another company already uses the same domain (or the same LinkedIn page when there is no domain). The later record is the duplicate. |
122	| `size_headcount_mismatch` | Headcount is outside the listed employee range (field `latest_headcount`), or revenue with that headcount implies more than $500,000 per employee (field `revenue_range`). Zero tolerance. |
123	
124	A record is `rejected` if it has no name, no domain and no LinkedIn page, or if it is a later duplicate. Any other issue makes it `flagged`. No issues means `valid`.
125	
126	### Facts and statuses (`src/core/data/facts.ts`, `src/core/types.ts`)
127	
128	Every fact carries a status, set by code only, and a provider.
129	
130	- Statuses: `given` (reported by the provider), `extracted`, `cross_checked` (agrees with other facts, with `derived_from` ids), `uncertain` (conflicting or unsupported).
131	- Providers: `crustdata`, `fixture`, `user_input`, `derived`, `model`.
132	
133	### The citeable rule
134	
135	A fact may be cited only if its status is `given` or `cross_checked` and its provider is not `model` (`isCiteableFact`).
136	
137	### validateAssessment and checkClaims (`src/core/agent/assessment-checks.ts`)
138	
139	Neither calls a model and neither changes a fact's status.
140	
141	- `validateAssessment` checks that `fit_score` and every criterion score are in 0 to 100, that each expected criterion is scored exactly once and nothing else is scored, and that every referenced fact id exists for the company. Referencing an `uncertain` fact is a warning.
142	- `checkClaims` checks an outreach draft. It must cite at least one fact. Every cited id must exist for the company, must not come from the model, and must have a citeable status. **Number check:** every number in the body must appear in a cited citeable fact, so an unknown figure cannot be stated as established (error code `unsupported_number`).
143	
144	## Safety and spend controls
145	
146	- **Caps.** `RunConfig` limits search results, enrichments, model calls per run (20) and output tokens per call (1500). The evidence runs use 10 searched and 5 enriched. Defaults are 100 and 15; the `dev` config uses 10 and 2.
147	- **Budget guard.** `BudgetGuard` is checked before every paid search and enrichment call in the Crustdata provider.
148	- **Spend flags.** The runner refuses `--provider crustdata` or `--llm real` without `--confirm-spend`, and checks that the needed key is present before anything is built.
149	- **Model usage limits.** The model-call count is the only per-run model usage cap, and the per-request output-token limit is also enforced. Dollar-denominated model spend caps and shared-key spend thresholds are not implemented: `src/core/agent/llm-policy.ts` states that both are "not yet agreed". The gateway key spend header is read and recorded, but nothing stops a run based on it.
150	- **Tracing is off for real-data runs.** `--trace on` with `--provider crustdata` is refused, and tracing is always off for Crustdata runs.
151	- **Reports hold counts and ids only.** Run reports in `runs/` contain counts, ids, costs, issue codes, tokens and timings. No company records, keys or headers.
152	- **Keys are never in the repo.** `.env` and `runs/` are git-ignored. Keys are read from environment variables.
153	
154	## Run it
155	
156	```bash
157	npm install
158	npm run dev          # Next.js dev server
159	```
160	
161	Runner: `npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline.ts [flags]`
162	
163	| Flag | Meaning |
164	|---|---|
165	| `--pipeline baseline\|improved` | Required. |
166	| `--llm fake\|real` | Default `fake`. `real` calls the LiteLLM gateway; needs `LITELLM_API_KEY` and `--confirm-spend`. |
167	| `--provider fixture\|crustdata` | Default `fixture`. `crustdata` needs `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` and `--confirm-spend`. |
168	| `--confirm-spend` | Required with `--llm real` or `--provider crustdata`. |
169	| `--label <string>` | Run label. Default is the pipeline name. |
170	| `--config dev\|eval` | Default `eval` (10 searched, 5 enriched). `dev` is 10 searched, 2 enriched. |
171	| `--trace on\|off` | Fixture runs only. Default on for fixture runs. Needs `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` to send traces. |
172	| `--industry`, `--country`, `--sizes` | Crustdata runs only. Defaults: `Staffing and Recruiting`, `India`, `11-50,51-200`. |
173	
174	Examples:
175	
176	```bash
177	# Free: fixtures, fake model, no network
178	npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline.ts --pipeline baseline --trace off
179	npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline.ts --pipeline improved --label dry --trace off
180	
181	# Costs model money: fixtures, real model through the gateway
182	npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline.ts --pipeline improved --llm real --confirm-spend --label improved-final
183	
184	# Costs provider money: real Crustdata data, fake model, tracing always off
185	npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline.ts --pipeline improved --provider crustdata --confirm-spend \
186	  --industry "Staffing and Recruiting" --country India --sizes 11-50,51-200
187	```
188	
189	Fixture versus Crustdata: fixture runs use synthetic records and simulate provider cost at measured prices (search 0.069 USD per record, enrichment 0.60 USD per company). Crustdata runs call the live API and spend real money.
190	
191	Cost summary:
192	
193	- No cost: `npm run dev`, `npm test`, fixture runs with the fake model.
194	- Costs model money: `--llm real`.
195	- Costs provider money: `--provider crustdata` (about 3.69 USD per run at the evaluation caps, measured).
196	
197	Each run writes `runs/<timestamp>-<label>.json`.
198	
199	## Results page
200	
201	Run `npm run dev`, then open http://localhost:3000/results.
202	
203	It shows:
204	
205	- The official fixture evidence, read from `evidence/summary.json`.
206	- The live-data validation counts, with their caveat.
207	- A separate synthetic guardrail demonstration. A deterministic fake model injects an unsupported number into one outreach, and the claim check suppresses it.
208	
209	Only synthetic mode is supported. Any other mode, for example `?mode=live`, is rejected on the server before anything is built. The page runs the real improved pipeline on fixtures with the fake model, makes no external calls and reads no environment variables. An import-guard test enforces this.
210	
211	`evidence/summary.json` is bundled at build time, so rebuild or restart the dev server after editing it.
212	
213	## Live beta (invite-only)
214	
215	The page at `/live` takes an invite code and a small ICP form, and runs the improved pipeline for that code. The server routes are `POST /api/live/run` (a run) and `GET /api/live/status` (whether live mode is switched on).
216	
217	### Status
218	
219	This paragraph is the one place to edit when the facts change.
220	
221	- The production deployment is at https://mindstack-neathack.vercel.app.
222	- Production now has the live variables configured (`CRUSTDATA_LIVE_API_KEY`, `LIVE_LLM_API_KEY`, `LIVE_LLM_BASE_URL`, `LIVE_LLM_MODEL`).
223	- Live mode stays off by default through the kill switch. It is switched on only for a builder-run test.
224	- After the first verified live run (below), every test code was disabled and the kill switch is off, so live mode is armed but closed.
225	- Only builder-only live codes can run live mode. None is enabled at the time of writing.
226	- Outsiders and judges get synthetic mode only.
227	- Third-party display of Crustdata records still waits for Crustdata's written confirmation.
228	- No company data from live runs is shown publicly. Demo evidence for live runs is limited to counts, costs and usage-page reconciliation.
229	
230	### First verified live run
231	
232	On 12 October 2026, around midday IST, one live run was made on the deployed site with a builder-only live code. The kill switch was on for the duration of the request and off again right after.
233	
234	| Measure | Value |
235	|---|---|
236	| Status | completed |
237	| Companies searched | 10 |
238	| Enriched | 5 |
239	| Assessed | 5 |
240	| Assessments failed | 0 |
241	| Outreach drafts kept | 5 |
242	| Outreach drafts suppressed | 0 |
243	| Provider cost estimate | 3.69 USD (10 searched at 0.069 plus 5 enriched at 0.60, basis `estimated_per_record`) |
244	| Model cost estimate | 0.0195 USD (basis `estimated`, complete; flat fallback rates of 1.10 and 5.50 USD per million input and output tokens, as in `src/core/agent/llm-policy.ts`) |
245	
246	- The `live_runs` table holds the same counts and costs and no company data.
247	- The model was `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Anthropic documents that endpoint as intended for testing and comparing models, not as a long-term production solution.
248	- **Reconciliation of provider cost.** Crustdata's Usage page showed 12.3 credits used on 12 October 2026, the only usage that day (3.69 USD at 0.30 USD per credit). Its API Keys page showed the dedicated key's budget at 87.7 of 100 afterwards.
249	- **Model cost is our estimate only.** The model provider's own usage page was not checked.
250	- **Before the run.** A free probe with an industry that matches nothing was refused with `invalid_request` and gave the run back (the code's run counter stayed unchanged). This confirmed the live keys were active.
251	- **Earlier local check.** `scripts/check-live-model.ts` had first run the improved pipeline on the fixtures with the real model: 5 assessed, 0 failed, 5052 input and 1177 output tokens.
252	- **Deployed page.** Garvit tested the deployed /live page with a synthetic code and checked its layout on his phone.
253	- This is one run. It is not a benchmark.
254	
255	### Modes
256	
257	Each invite code is bound to one mode, set by whoever creates it (default `synthetic`).
258	
259	- **synthetic.** Fixture companies and a fake model. The search criteria you enter are ignored (the response says so), and nothing is spent. One outreach draft deliberately contains an injected unsupported number so the claim check can be seen suppressing it.
260	- **live.** Real Crustdata data and a real model (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the first verified run), for the builders only. A live run searches up to 10 companies, enriches up to 5, and allows up to 20 model calls and 1500 output tokens per call. The search is sorted by company id ascending. The industry you type is matched to the first autocomplete suggestion from Crustdata, and the response says which industry was searched.
261	
262	The form accepts an industry of 2 to 80 characters, the country India, and the sizes 11-50 and 51-200. Codes are up to 64 characters.
263	
264	### How a run is protected
265	
266	- **Hashed codes.** Codes are stored as HMAC-SHA256 hashes keyed with `INVITE_HMAC_SECRET` (at least 32 characters). Codes are normalised first (case, dashes and spaces ignored). Generated codes are 32 characters from a 160-bit random value.
267	- **One atomic reservation.** A run is reserved with a single conditional database update that increments the use count only if the code exists, is enabled, has runs left and is not locked.
268	- **One run at a time per code.** The reservation sets a lock that lasts 330 seconds. It is cleared when the run finishes or is given back. A second request while the lock is held gets `run_in_progress` (HTTP 409).
269	- **Give-back.** If a live run fails before the first paid call, the reservation is released and the run is not counted. A live run that fails after that is counted.
270	- **Per-IP rate limits.** 20 run requests per 60 seconds per IP. 5 wrong-code attempts per 900 seconds per IP (an unknown or disabled code counts). 60 status requests per 60 seconds per IP. IPs are stored only as HMAC hashes. Windows are fixed windows, not sliding.
271	- **Body limit.** A request body over 4096 bytes, a non-JSON content type or invalid JSON gets the fixed `invalid_request` body.
272	- **Fixed error bodies.** Every error response uses a fixed message chosen by status code. No thrown-error text, stack trace, key, code or upstream text is returned. Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.
273	- **Scrubbing.** Free-text fields in a pipeline result (issue messages, failed-assessment messages, validation reasons, check findings, the run description) are replaced by fixed text chosen by code, once on the server and again when the results are mapped for the page.
274	- **Logging.** The application code does not log request bodies, invite codes or results. The hosting platform keeps its standard request logs (method, path and status), which we checked contain no bodies.
275	- **No company data stored.** The database holds invite codes (hash, label, run limits, mode), one row per run with counts and costs only, a settings table and rate-limit counters.
276	- **Kill switch.** A `live_enabled` setting, off by default in the schema. While it is off, live-mode codes get `live_disabled` (HTTP 503) and the run is given back. Synthetic codes never read it. A live run is also refused when the live keys are not configured.
277	- **Tracing is off for real-data runs.** The live path does not use neatlogs.
278	
279	### How costs are reported
280	
281	Every run response carries a cost block.
282	
283	- **Provider cost.** In synthetic mode it is simulated at fixture prices (`simulated_fixture_prices`). In live mode it is an estimate from the records searched and enriched at the measured per-record prices (`estimated_per_record`). It is never an invoice. The Crustdata usage page is the source of truth for charges.
284	- **Model cost.** `model_usd` is the known model cost only. `model_basis` says where the known costs came from: `none` (no external model cost, always so in synthetic mode), `gateway_reported`, `estimated` (from token usage at fallback rates), `mixed`, or `unavailable` (model calls were made but none has a known cost). `model_complete` is true only when every model call has a known cost; when it is false, `model_usd` is a lower bound. A model cost of 0 with basis `unavailable` means unknown, not free.
285	
286	### Deployment
287	
288	The deployment target is Vercel Hobby with a Neon Postgres database.
289	
290	Environment variable names:
291	
292	| Name | Needed for |
293	|---|---|
294	| `DATABASE_URL` | Required. Postgres connection for the live routes and the admin script. |
295	| `INVITE_HMAC_SECRET` | Required. At least 32 characters. Used for code and IP hashes. |
296	| `CRUSTDATA_LIVE_API_KEY` | Optional. Live mode only. |
297	| `LIVE_LLM_API_KEY` | Optional. Live mode only. |
298	| `LIVE_LLM_BASE_URL` | Optional. Live mode only. |
299	| `LIVE_LLM_MODEL` | Optional. Live mode only. When absent, the model in the code's live run config is used. |
300	
301	Without `DATABASE_URL` and `INVITE_HMAC_SECRET` the routes answer `live_unavailable`. If any of the three optional variables is missing, live mode is off and synthetic codes still run. Production has the live keys configured. Live mode stays closed by the kill switch except during a builder-run test.
302	
303	Setup:
304	
305	1. Apply `src/server/live/schema.sql` to the database with any Postgres client. It is idempotent and can be applied more than once. It creates the tables and sets `live_enabled` to `false`.
306	2. Create codes and manage them with the admin script, which needs `DATABASE_URL` and `INVITE_HMAC_SECRET` in the environment. A new code is printed once, when it is created.
307	
308	```bash
309	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts create --label <label> --runs <n> [--mode synthetic|live]
310	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts set-mode --label <label> --mode synthetic|live
311	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts list
312	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts disable --label <label>
313	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts enable --label <label>
314	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts add-runs --label <label> --n <n>
315	npx tsx scripts/live-admin.ts kill-switch on|off|status
316	```
317	
318	`kill-switch off` stops live-mode codes; `kill-switch on` allows them (only if the live keys are also configured).
319	
320	### Tested
321	
322	- The unit suite last ran with 741 passed and 6 skipped (`npm test`).
323	- An integration test (`tests/live/pg-store.integration.test.ts`) fires 20 parallel run reservations at one code on a managed Postgres and lets exactly one through; the other 19 get `run_in_progress`. It ran once, from a laptop, against a development branch of the managed database. It is skipped unless `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set, which is why the suite reports one skipped file and 6 skipped tests (the file holds six tests). It runs in a throwaway schema that is dropped afterwards.
324	
325	## Tests
326	
327	```bash
328	npm test        # vitest run
329	npm run lint
330	```
331	
332	Tests are in `tests/` (validation, facts, providers, runner metrics) and `tests/agent/` (pipelines, assessment checks, citation metrics, prompts, gateway client, cost handling). They make no network calls.
333	
334	## Tools used
335	
336	- **neatlogs** records traces of the fixture runs. The Markdown exports are in `evidence/traces/`.
337	- **Entire** records checkpoints of the work; the commit trailers are listed in `hackathon.md`.
338	- **cfo.ai** holds the business plan, a hypothetical model whose figures other than the measured unit costs are assumptions.
339	- **Crustdata** is the company data provider for search and enrichment.
340	- **LiteLLM gateway** is the OpenAI-compatible endpoint used for model calls.
341	
342	## Repository layout
343	
344	| Path | Contents | Primary contributors (approx., by commit history) |
345	|---|---|---|
346	| `src/app/` | Next.js frontend: ICP form, results | Garvit Mathur (mostly) |
347	| `src/core/agent/` | Pipelines, prompts, assessment checks, model clients | Garvit Mathur (mostly); Abhijit Manna for cost, tracing and metrics |
348	| `src/core/data/` | Validation, facts, providers, budget guard | Abhijit Manna |
349	| `src/core/fixtures/` | Synthetic companies | Abhijit Manna |
350	| `src/core/observability/` | neatlogs setup | Abhijit Manna |
351	| `scripts/` | Runner and smoke scripts | Abhijit Manna |
352	| `tests/` | Unit tests | Both; mostly Abhijit Manna |
353	| `evidence/` | `summary.json` and trace exports | Abhijit Manna |
354	| `runs/` | Local run reports (git-ignored) | n/a |
355	
356	Ownership is taken from commit counts per folder, not from a formal assignment.
357	
358	## Limitations
359	
360	- The fixtures are synthetic.
361	- Provider cost in fixture runs is simulated at measured prices.
362	- The size rule has zero tolerance and the magnitude of the mismatches was not analysed.
363	- There is one scenario.
364	- The first live-data run used a fake model. A second pair of live runs used the real model through the hackathon gateway, which means real company profiles were sent to that gateway. Each is a single run on 10 companies.
365	- A neatlogs processing incident on Oct 11 was resolved the same day.
366	- No per-run model cost cap or shared-key spend threshold is enforced (see Safety and spend controls).
367	- Live beta: the per-run model cost cap and the key budget threshold are not implemented (same gap as above). A live run is bounded only by the call and record caps and the per-code run limit.
368	- Live beta: the first verified live run is a single run. The model cost is our estimate at flat fallback rates; the model provider's usage page was not checked. Anthropic documents its OpenAI-compatible endpoint as intended for testing and comparing models, not as a long-term production solution.
369	- Live beta: `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` has a tentative retirement date not sooner than 15 October 2026, according to Anthropic's model status page as checked on 12 October 2026.
370	- Live beta: Anthropic's documentation says Claude 4.7 and later models return an error for a non-default temperature, and our client always sends temperature 0; claude-haiku-5-5 is a later model, so we expect it to be affected, but we did not test it.
371	- Live beta: there is no alerting and no admin UI. Codes and the kill switch are managed with the admin script.
372	- Live beta: the rate limit uses the first of `x-real-ip`, then `x-forwarded-for`. On Vercel the platform sets both and, per Vercel's request-headers documentation, overwrites `x-forwarded-for` to prevent spoofing. On any other host these headers could be spoofed.
373	- Run reports are local and not committed, so the numbers in `evidence/summary.json` cannot be re-derived from the repo alone.
374	- The Crustdata provider retries HTTP requests (up to 2 retries on 429, 5xx and network errors) inside its post method without rechecking the budget before each retry, so a retry after a lost response could repeat a billable call, up to three attempts for one chunk. We did not observe this: the Crustdata usage page matched our expected credits exactly after the real runs, but we did not log HTTP attempts. Budget checks happen once per logical operation (before each search and before each enrichment chunk).
375	
376	## Team

SHORT REVIEW REPORT

Only README.md changed. I ran git status only, and did not read .env.

What changed (line numbers are approximate, from the edit locations):
- Lines 225-228, Status paragraph:
  - I replaced "Only builder-only live codes… / Outsiders and judges get synthetic mode only" with your wording. It covers the codes, the synthetic public demo code, live mode off by default, and no live code enabled.
  - I replaced the "written confirmation" line with the 12 October question, the same-day informal reply, and the pending follow-up.
- Line ~277, Safety section: "No company data stored." is now "Data handling." with your exact replacement text, followed by the existing description of what the database holds.
- Line ~324, Tested: 741 changed to 808 passed and 6 skipped, with a note that the 6 are the Postgres tests needing TEST_DATABASE_URL.
- Limitations list (before the "Run reports are local" item): added the item that the first question to Crustdata did not mention the model provider or a public demo video, and that the follow-up reply is pending.
- Line 215, Live beta intro: added the sentence on no export or download, at most 10 companies per run, and a few runs per code.
- The repository README had no other "waits for written confirmation" statement, and I did not touch hackathon.md.

CLAIMS I COULD NOT VERIFY (all taken from your facts, not from files):
- The 12 October exchange with Crustdata, the informal reply, and the pending follow-up.
- "Each live code is capped at a few runs" and "no export or download feature". I did not check the code for either.
- "Results are returned only to the requesting browser, and our code does not log them." This is your wording; the README's Logging bullet says similar, but I did not check it against the code.
- The 808 passed / 6 skipped count.

Unsure about:
- Line 260 (Modes, live) still says "for the builders only", which now conflicts with live codes going to invited testers. I kept it as instructed.
- Lines 78-80 say "company records are never stored" and "No company record is stored in the repository, in the run reports or in any trace". They are narrower than the phrase you named, so I kept them.
- Line 228 says no live-run company data is "shown publicly", and the Crustdata reply allows showing it to invited testers. I kept the line because it is about public display.
- Your wording says the criteria are sent "to Crustdata". Elsewhere the README says "Crustdata" for the provider, so this matches.
